one_liner: Pure-Rust FLAC encoder and decoder claiming 17% faster encode and 23% faster decode than FFmpeg 8.1.2's flac.
what_it_does: Encodes and decodes native FLAC entirely in Rust with no C and no required dependencies (no_std plus alloc capable). The encoder buffers a whole stream: Encoder::new(rate, channels, bps) for 8/16/24-bit and up to 8 channels, push_planar / push_interleaved / push_s16le_bytes / push_f32le_bytes, then finish() returns the complete file (fLaC marker, STREAMINFO with MD5, frames; no other metadata). The decoder works over a complete in-memory &[u8]: Decoder::next_frame appends planar i32 per frame, and decode() is the one-call form. It is its own Rust API, not a libFLAC or libavcodec drop-in; inside remade_ffmpeg_rs it backs the rff CLI's FLAC codec.
how_it_is_fast: The encoder does a two-phase, estimate-gated search per fixed 4,096-sample block: every stereo arm (left, right, mid, side) gets a cheap estimate (exact integer autocorrelation over Q15 Tukey windows 0.5 and 0.2, Levinson-Durbin, one-pass fixed-order |residual| sums), and only arms whose stereo mode is within a margin of the best estimate are realized with real residuals and an exact Rice plan. The Rice planner merges partition sums bottom-up so every partition order (to 8) and both Rice and Rice2 are costed in one pass instead of a per-parameter scan, and four runtime-detected AVX2 kernels (autocorrelation, Rice sums, fixed-order sums, FMA LPC residual) sit beside scalar twins; an accumulator bit writer, table CRCs and an unrolled MD5 cut the rest. The decoder uses a 64-bit left-aligned bit reader refilled a word at a time, leading_zeros Rice reads with one refill, and const-generic LPC restore loops for orders 1-12. FFmpeg's level 8, by contrast, uses 4,608-sample blocks at 44.1 kHz, Levinson LPC with its 4-level order search and an estimated stereo mode (libavcodec/flacenc.c), so the two encoders search different spaces.
when_to_use: Rust services, desktop apps or WASM builds that need FLAC encode and decode with no C toolchain and no LGPL code (Apache-2.0); RAG Converter uses it in the browser.

no_std microcontroller encoders: the README reports about 15-20 ms per 4,096-sample 16 kHz mono block on an ESP32-S3 at 240 MHz and a byte-gated peak heap of about 124 KB for an 8,192-sample stream (first-party).

Whole-file encoding of 8/16/24-bit PCM (up to 8 channels) that libFLAC or FFmpeg will later decode; round trips are gated against claxon in tests and against FFmpeg in remade_ffmpeg_rs tools/flac_gate.ps1.
Devices that close one file per chunk (for example one second of audio): Encoder::finish_and_reset keeps buffers and window tables and gives bytes identical to a fresh encoder.
Decoding trusted 16- or 24-bit FLAC already in memory from Rust code that previously used claxon.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ projects: there is no C API, so you would need an FFI shim, and the comparison was against FFmpeg's flac, not libFLAC, which was never timed.

Untrusted input through decode(): it reserves Vec::with_capacity(total_samples) per channel straight from the 36-bit STREAMINFO field. Issue #9 (a 42-byte stream can request 80 GB and abort the process) was closed on 2026-09-15, but that line is still in src/decode.rs at HEAD (v0.2.0). Use Decoder::next_frame with your own bounded buffers, or check total_samples against the input length first.

Real-world files with ID3v2 prefixes, trailing tags or damaged frames, or Ogg FLAC: the decoder requires fLaC at byte 0, a bad sync, CRC-8 or CRC-16 returns an error, and decode() gives up on the whole stream instead of resynchronising.

32-bit FLAC: the README says 4-32-bit decode, but 32-bit stereo side channels need 33 bits while BitReader::read_bits/read_signed are written for n <= 32 and samples are i32. The gate matrix tests only 8, 16 and 24 bits, and 32-bit encode is a roadmap item.

Large or streaming jobs and tagging workflows: the encoder holds the whole input as i32 before finish(), the decoder needs the whole file in memory, there is no seeking, and no seek table, Vorbis comment, picture or padding block is written.

integration.dependencies: none required; optional libm (pure Rust) for no_std; dev-dependencies claxon and rusty_alloc-api
integration.platforms: any Rust target; Windows, Linux and macOS build and test per the README; no_std checked in CI on riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf and thumbv7em-none-eabihf; runs on ESP32-S3; AVX2/FMA kernels only on x86-64 with the std feature (runtime-detected)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Encoder and Decoder own their scratch buffers (the old thread-local pools were folded into each encoder) and the crate has only constant tables, so separate instances can run on separate threads; encoding of one stream is single-threaded.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the rff CLI of remade_ffmpeg_rs replaces ffmpeg's FLAC encode and decode with this code; as a library it is a different API from libavcodec or libFLAC

gotchas: Output carries only STREAMINFO (no Vorbis comment, no padding), so tag editors must rewrite the whole file; that missing 8,192-byte PADDING block is most of the README's 'smaller on 20/20' headline against FFmpeg.

Encoded bytes changed in 0.2.0 (integer autocorrelation); the CHANGELOG says to pin one version wherever two builds must agree byte for byte, and to enable the libm feature on the host for host-chip byte identity.
The decoder parses the STREAMINFO MD5 but never computes it; only frame CRC-8 and CRC-16 are checked.

unsafe is confined to four #[target_feature(enable = "avx2")] kernels, each with a bit-identity test against its scalar twin; the in-repo flacbench example hard-codes 44,100 Hz and runs under the org's rusty_alloc global allocator, which the project says is required for comparable numbers.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Symphonia (decode-only, multi-format, single-threaded tables against FFmpeg's native decoders) or flacenc-rs (encoder only, measured against the libFLAC flac 1.4.3 CLI) when you want one dependency-free Apache-2.0 crate that both encodes and decodes FLAC, including no_std encoding on a microcontroller. For decoding untrusted or messy real-world files, or when the comparison you care about is libFLAC rather than FFmpeg's flac, those siblings or libFLAC itself are the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README numbers on an unnamed Windows x86-64 machine with an unstated rustc and flags: both binaries pinned to one core, process CPU time, 31 ABBA pairs on one 180 s 44.1 kHz stereo music clip, encode at -compression_level 8 672 ms vs 813 ms and decode of an FFmpeg-encoded stream 266 ms vs 344 ms against the prebuilt Gyan FFmpeg 8.1.2 full_build. The timing harness, the clip and the command lines are still not public (remade_ffmpeg_rs tools/bench holds only codec-bench.ps1, pinab.py and unrelated scripts on 2026-10-04), so it is unknown whether process start-up, WAV/file I/O and, for the FFmpeg arm, the per-frame hand-offs between the demux, decode, filter, encode and mux threads that FFmpeg 7.0+ runs (all time-sliced on the one pinned core) are cancelled, as the sister rusty-opus harness's 300 s minus 150 s slope does for start-up; the smaller-file claim mostly reflects FFmpeg's default padding block, and level 8 means different search work in the two encoders.
status_note: Active but very young (49 commits, last commit 2026-10-04 bumping the README banner, v0.2.0 on 2026-09-30, a v0.2.1 release PR open); Apache-2.0 and dependency-free, so easy to vendor, but it has 1 star and the README's '1,358 Active Installs' banner equals the crates.io total download count (1,358), not a measured install base.
